engine.title: The multibagger screen qualified nobody for four weeks
engine.body: Corrects what this entry said on 2026-08-27. It read ‘the scan is running on schedule’ and blamed the fixed list on cadence. The ledger says otherwise: the last multibagger row is 2026-08-01, while magic, magicmagic and ai_longterm — the same Saturday job, the same slot — all logged 2026-08-22. Twenty-six days, three Saturdays, nothing written.
engine.note: The screen is not broken. Run on 2026-08-27 it took 11 candidates and rejected 10 for R:R below 2.0 — CHENNPETRO 1.29, FLUOROCHEM 1.07, GLAXO 0.59, which needs a 63% win rate merely to break even. The defect was that a week qualifying nobody wrote nothing at all, so the page served the 1 August list as though it were current. The attempt is recorded either way now. The gate is NOT loosened: publishing a 0.59 R:R to keep the section busy is the exact trade this screen exists to refuse, and an empty week is a real result.

engine.title: Stop buying strength that has already run
engine.body: The 4H RSI ceiling for longs was 75. Splitting every closed trade by the RSI recorded at entry showed the engine bleeding above 65 and profitable below it. The ceiling is now 65.
engine.note: Holds in both halves of the sample and at every cut point tested (60, 65, 70), so it is not one lucky threshold. The threshold was still chosen from this sample, so treat the size as an upper bound.

engine.title: A break-even stop would not have helped
engine.body: The median losing trade was +1.44R in profit before it reversed, and 59% touched a full +1R first. That looks like an obvious fix: move the stop to entry once price pays 1R. Re-walking every trade bar by bar, with winners subject to the same rule, says otherwise.
engine.note: The first version of this test only altered losers, which guarantees a positive answer. Correcting it reversed the conclusion. Nothing tested cleared one standard error, so no stop rule was adopted.

engine.title: Trades were being closed at prices that never traded
engine.body: The grader had never resolved a single trade — an exception was being swallowed silently — leaving a fallback path that could book an exit at a bar from before the signal existed. Every closed trade was re-graded against bars that actually printed.
evidence: exits corrected to a real price
engine.note: This moved the headline number against me. It is published anyway, because the earlier number was not real. Pre-correction data is kept in the repo rather than deleted.

engine.title: A first target must pay back the risk
engine.body: T1 was whichever structural level sat nearest the entry, with no distance test. One signal shipped a T1 worth 0.19R against its own stop, printed beside an R:R of 2.41 quoted off T2. T1 must now return at least 1R.

chess.title: Time Management
chess.body: Chess is a timed game. Use 70-80% of your clock in complex positions, blitz transitions and endgames you know. Common mistake: spending 15 minutes in the opening, then rushing in the critical middlegame. Rule: if a position is complicated and you see candidate moves, spend the time here — not in simple positions. Clock is a resource, not just a constraint.

wisdom.title: Being a Better Husband
wisdom.body: The best fathers are also good partners. Your daughter watches how you treat her mother. That becomes her template for relationships. Simple acts: say thank you. Notice when your partner is tired. Take something off her plate without being asked. Ask about her day and actually listen. Small but it compounds.

book.author: Jim Collins
book.chapter: The Flywheel: No Single Defining Action
book.lesson: No good-to-great company had a single defining moment, a killer strategy launch, or a magic programme. Instead, the transformation always followed a flywheel pattern: push the heavy flywheel, it barely moves, keep pushing consistently in one direction, it builds momentum, eventually it reaches a breakthrough — but there was no single push that did it. The mistake most organisations make is looking for the one big thing. The reality is thousands of consistent small things, all pointing the same direction, that eventually produce dramatic results.
book.key_quote: Sustainable success is built through consistent, compounding effort — not single dramatic breakthroughs.
book.action: Identify your flywheel: what is the core loop in your career or business that, if pushed consistently, would build unstoppable momentum?
crux: Good is the enemy of great. Most organisations never become great because they become good enough.
Level 5 Leadership: extreme personal humility combined with intense professional will.
First Who, Then What. Get the right people on the bus before setting direction.
Confront the brutal facts while never losing faith — the Stockdale Paradox.
The Hedgehog Concept: the intersection of what you're deeply passionate about, what you can be best in the world at, and what drives your economics.
One economic denominator — profit per X — clarifies the entire business.
A culture of discipline, not a tyrant imposing discipline.
Technology accelerates momentum; it never creates it.
The Flywheel: relentless pushing in a consistent direction until momentum compounds.
The Doom Loop is the opposite — new programmes, new directions, no accumulation.
Great companies had no miracle moment. Transformation looked dramatic only from outside.
Stop-doing lists matter more than to-do lists.
Compensation gets the right people on the bus; it does not motivate the wrong ones.
learnings: Who beats what. Wrong people make the right strategy fail.
Facing bad news early is a competitive advantage.
Momentum accumulates from consistent direction, not from bursts of intensity.
Greatness is mostly a series of unglamorous, consistent decisions.
examples: Walgreens beat the market 15x from 1975–2000 by fixating on profit per customer visit — one metric, relentlessly.
Darwin Smith at Kimberly-Clark sold the paper mills — the company's historic core — to enter consumer paper against P&G. Shareholder returns beat the market 4x.
Nucor's flywheel: mini-mill technology → lower cost → market share → more mills. Same push for decades.
adapt: Hedgehog: CA precision + FP&A + building with AI. That intersection is narrower and stronger than 'finance content'.
Economic denominator for Codex: profit per customer, not downloads.
Brutal fact: 1H signals have no measurable edge. Faith: the daily equity engine does. Hold both.
Stop-doing list beats the roadmap. Deleting three TradeFlow pages was the flywheel push.

minimalism.title: The Box Test
minimalism.body: Pack a category into a box and seal it. If you have not opened it in a month, you do not need what is inside. Most people cannot name the contents a week later.
minimalism.action: Box one category — cables, kitchen gadgets, old chargers. Date the box.
minimalism.label: Minimalism

etiquette.title: Say The Difficult Thing Kindly And Once
etiquette.body: Softening it into unrecognisability is not kindness — it guarantees you say it again, worse, later. Direct and warm. Once.
etiquette.action: Name one thing you have been avoiding saying. Say it plainly today.
etiquette.label: Etiquette

stillness.title: Do One Thing At A Time
stillness.body: The monastic instruction is: when walking, walk; when eating, eat. Multitasking is the belief that attention divides without loss. It does not.
stillness.action: Do the next task with nothing else open.
stillness.label: Stillness

model.title: Opportunity Cost
model.body: The real cost of anything is the best alternative you gave up. Cash sitting idle has a cost. So does a meeting. So does a project you keep alive out of habit.
model.action: Name what your largest time commitment is displacing.
model.label: Mental Model

arabic.label: Arabic

drill.title: Reverse-Engineer A Good Model
drill.body: Take a model you admire and rebuild its structure from scratch. Copying output teaches nothing; reconstructing the logic teaches everything.
drill.action: Rebuild one section of a model you did not write.
drill.label: Drill

health.title: Sleep Is The Performance Lever
health.body: Under 7 hours measurably degrades reaction time, glucose control, immune function, and emotional regulation. One night at 4 hours drops next-day insulin sensitivity by around 25%. You cannot out-discipline this.
health.action: Fixed lights-out tonight. Same time tomorrow.
health.label: Health

quote.name: Arianna Huffington
quote.quote: Fearlessness is not the absence of fear. It's making the decision that something else is more important than fear.

lesson.lesson: You become what you give your attention to.

case.title: Amazon: AWS — the accidental trillion-dollar business
case.story: Amazon built AWS to solve internal infrastructure problems. They then sold the solution to the world. AWS now generates $90B+ revenue per year.
case.lesson: Your internal problems are often external opportunities. The best products are built to scratch your own itch.

fpna.title: Driver-Based Forecasting
fpna.body: Build forecasts on business drivers (units, headcount, utilization), not historical % growth.

cfo.title: FC Interview: Top 5 Questions
cfo.body: 1. Walk me through month-end close. 2. How do you handle a material variance? 3. What internal controls have you implemented? 4. Describe your IFRS 16 experience. 5. How do you present bad news to management? Prepare 2-min answers for all five.

money_hack.title: SIP on Salary Day
money_hack.body: Set SIP date = salary day + 1. Invest before you spend. Pay yourself first.

dubai.title: The visa question, answered
dubai.body: Employment visa is sponsored by the employer — you do not need one to apply, and any recruiter asking you to pay for one is running a scam. The Golden Visa needs a AED 30K+ salary and a degree attestation, which is exactly why AED 30K is the threshold worth targeting.
dubai.targets: Attest the degree in India first. It takes 3–6 weeks and blocks everything downstream.
dubai.action: MEA attestation on the CA certificate and the degree. Before an offer, not after.

desk.productivity: Phone in another room during deep work. Physical distance reduces urge 60%.

father.title: Offer food she can hold
father.do: Soft strips she can grip herself — steamed carrot, banana, well-cooked pasta. Accept the mess.
father.why: Self-feeding at 7 months develops the pincer grip and, more importantly, lets her control intake. Children who regulate their own portions early are less likely to over-eat later.

father.title: Protect the sleep routine
father.do: Same order, same lighting, same time — bath, feed, book, bed. Do it yourself at least twice a week.
father.why: Consistency of sequence matters more than the exact timing. Fathers who own bedtime regularly build a distinct attachment relationship rather than a substitute one.

life_wisdom.teaching: Seeing things as they are, before preference distorts them. The first of the three jewels, and deliberately placed before right conduct.
life_wisdom.apply: Separate the number from what you want the number to be. Write the actual result before writing the explanation — the order changes the explanation.

life_wisdom.teaching: The Buddha's image: struck by an arrow, most people fire a second one into themselves — the story about what the first arrow means.
life_wisdom.apply: A stopped-out trade is the first arrow. 'I am bad at this' is the second. Only one of them was caused by the market.

speaking.title: End the sentence
speaking.drill: Read three sentences aloud and drop your pitch on the final word of each. Record and check you are not rising at the end.
speaking.why: Upward inflection turns statements into questions. It is the fastest way to sound unsure of numbers you are certain about.

interview_tech.q: Explain deferred tax to a board member in 60 seconds.
interview_tech.a: Accounting profit and taxable profit are computed under different rules, so tax paid this year rarely matches tax on this year's reported profit. Deferred tax records the future consequence of that gap. The classic retail example is accelerated capital allowances on fit-out: you get the tax relief early, so you owe more tax later — that future obligation sits as a deferred tax liability. It is not cash and it is not a provision for a dispute; it is timing. Say that last sentence, because it is what they are actually worried about.

interview_tech.q: How do you measure promotional effectiveness properly?
interview_tech.a: Incremental margin, not uplift. Take the sales during the promotion, subtract what the baseline would have been without it, subtract the margin given away on units that would have sold at full price anyway, and subtract any cannibalisation of adjacent full-price lines. The result is often negative for deep discounts on already-popular SKUs. Use a control group of comparable stores where operationally possible — without a counterfactual, every promotion looks successful because sales always rise.

interview_soft.q: What would your last manager say is your weakness?
interview_soft.a: Name a real one with a boundary. The pattern that works: a genuine weakness, evidence you know its cost, and the specific mechanism you use to contain it. 'I go too deep into detail before surfacing a view — it has cost me time on low-stakes analysis. I now set a decision deadline before starting and present at that point regardless of how complete it feels.' Avoid perfectionism, avoid anything that would disqualify you for the role itself.

interview_soft.q: What is the hardest decision you have made in your career?
interview_soft.a: Hard means genuinely two-sided, not merely unpleasant. Redundancies, closing a site, overruling someone you respected, or choosing between two people for one role. Structure: the trade-off, the information you had and did not have, how you decided, what it cost, and what you would do differently. Interviewers discount any answer where the right choice was obvious in hindsight — say what made it genuinely close.
